pra_nam_A_lexical.authority: MW L131079 gives P and Ā; Bhāgavata 10.64.42 attests 1sg Ā with accusative viprān. Apte L22272 labels the lemma P.

pari_nam_A_lexical.role: subject undergoing change, ripening, or turning aside as appropriate to the source
pari_nam_A_lexical.authority: MW L117520 and Apte L20195 list both padas; Apte adduces pariṇamate in a transformation context.

nam_karmakartari_rod.role: the rod which would be bent is itself presented as performing the change
nam_karmakartari_rod.authority: Kāśikā 3.1.87 and 3.1.89; yak/ciṇ blocked for nam in this construction.

nam_karmani_rod.role: the rod is the expressed patient of an external agent’s bending
nam_karmani_rod.authority: 1.3.13, 3.1.67 and 3.1.66. Named-root exclusion of 3.1.89 belongs to karmakartari.

role_diagnostics.agentive_lexical_middle: In the Bhāgavata, aham is the person bowing and viprān is the accusative plural designating the recipients. The root has a middle ending in a transitive worship construction in that verse. Converting this to a passive or self-bending rod analysis would lose both participants. The following namata addresses yūyam in P.
role_diagnostics.karmakartari: In the commentarial example the event can be predicated of the rod itself, svayam eva. The ordinary transfer of patient-like operations under 3.1.87 is qualified: nam lacks yak and ciṇ under 3.1.89 but retains middle endings. The Kāśikā prints both namate and anaṃsta in full clauses. In the unsuffixed description a causal sense can be implicit, as explained in the Śabdakaustubha.
role_diagnostics.karmani: The expression of a real patient takes yak in the sārvadhātuka present-domain and ciṇ in aorist 3sg. In the other third-person aorists the common sic-middle forms no longer distinguish the two histories.

source_boundaries: Lexical P/Ā headings are source-specific; the Bhāgavata line is evidence for its actual first singular. The grammatical schedules are licensed extensions within the indicated lexical register.
